project.title: Fleetdesk rental management
project.alt: Actual Fleetdesk quotation for a synthetic three-day rental with a saved 204 euro example total
project.desc: Quote a rental, allocate an available vehicle and manage demonstration reservations with tested date, pricing and concurrency rules.
project.built: Extended the original vehicle/customer application with genuine synthetic reservations, advisory availability, quotation snapshots, cancellation and completion while preserving its existing REST contracts.
project.why: A rental workspace must prevent two customers from being promised the same vehicle for overlapping dates, and keep the reviewed price clear when records change.
how: Choose an existing customer, a vehicle and a UTC collection/return period, then review the calculated quote.
Confirm an allocation with overlap and current-rate checks; retry safely if a response is lost.
Track active, upcoming and return-due reservations, cancel allocations or complete due rentals, and inspect calculated availability.
project.demonstrates: Full-stack development, REST endpoints, relational data access and translating a record-management requirement into a usable interface.
project.caption: Genuine shared-frontend quotation: three days at €68 per day gives €204. Confirmation rechecks both rate and allocation. Synthetic records; no actual rental or payment.
project.result: Existing record workflows and new rental workflows pass API/domain, browser-rule and full browser checks before this release. The isolated MySQL integration verifies simultaneous overlap rejection, retry identity, saved prices, referential integrity and state transitions. Desktop/mobile captures match this exact source revision; the linked run records its actual result.
project.limits: Synthetic educational application, with no real fleet, payments, tax/deposit calculation or deployed multi-user backend. The public demo is local to one browser profile and uses Web Locks to coordinate its tabs; it cannot allocate across devices. UTC dates use an exclusive return date. Early-return pricing, rental amendments and deletion of referenced history are outside scope. MySQL allocation safety assumes writes use the transactional service.
project.technical: Separate pure rental rules, memory/MySQL adapters and a presentation module preserve original CRUD routes. Python and JavaScript follow a 27-case rules contract. Memory uses a shared RLock; browser writes use an exclusive Web Lock and fresh storage read; MySQL confirmation locks the vehicle/customer rows in a transaction and preserves references with foreign keys. Request IDs prevent duplicate creation after a lost response. Integer-cent rate and name snapshots preserve quoted terms; stale rates require a new quote.
project.run: Install requirements.txt; set DEMO_MODE=1 and run python CarServer.py. The README documents the non-destructive MySQL reservation migration and opt-in isolated integration checks. The public static demo shares its frontend and tested rules contract.
gallery: Calculated availability for a selected period, with active, upcoming and return-due counts.
Actual reservation snapshots, lifecycle actions and an accurate saved example price.
The real mobile rental form, with a scrollable quotation and confirmation controls.
Original inventory and customer editing remain available.
project.demo_disclosure: Public demo: browser-managed synthetic data. The Flask/MySQL implementation is available separately in the source.
project.challenge: Availability can change between viewing a quote and confirming it. The solution rechecks at the write boundary: a process lock, a browser Web Lock or a MySQL transaction serializes competing allocations. A concurrent test must produce one successful reservation and one conflict, while an identical retry returns the original record.
